findings: All paragraph boundaries retained: 72,45,42,40,38 per language. Episode 02 paragraph16 strong emphasis retained; all quote-only paragraphs preserved separately.

Episode01: refusal as a real answer, relationship penalties, personal limits versus coercion, temporary delegation versus permanent control, and emergency intervention limited to immediate danger with later explanation/challenge/correction and prompt return of decision-making were checked.

Episode02: good intention does not confer ownership of another life; stability/exploration, speed/composure and failure/decision trade-offs retained. Children, severe incapacity, imminent danger and temporary loss of clear judgment retained without added conditions; return of decision-making preserved.
Episode03: practical delegation is distinguished from removing judgment; no silent repair to paragraph23. Shared serious consequences and refusal to assume unlimited outcomes remain explicit.

Episode04: gratitude is not compulsory use; both refusal of help and cessation of help remain possible. Emergency scope and necessity are bounded, and post-emergency explanation, questions and return of decisions are retained.

Episode05: no claim that suffering is inherently valuable; preventable destructive harm must not be allowed for a lesson. Shared consequences, finite support, and protection aimed at regained capability rather than sustained dependence are retained.

Writer refined FR03 paragraphs24/29 for oscillation and judgment wording; FR01 paragraph47 for unambiguous purpose; FR02 paragraph34 to preserve the other person as an end rather than merely their welfare. No source text changed.
